subject: English L1
title: Unit 4: Past Simple and Time Clauses

A.q: When I blank a kid, I blank football.
A.explain: Correct is was / played. Were is plural. Play is present. Didn't played is double past.

A.q: My high-school friends always blank parties.
A.explain: Past simple is had. Has is present. Are having is continuous. Did not had is incorrect.

A.q: My brothers and I blank in Dubai in 2000.
A.explain: Plural subject needs were. Was is singular. There were and there was are existential.

A.q: Kate blank her leg when she fell down.
A.explain: Simple past is broke. Break is present. Broken is participle. Breaking is continuous.

A.q: I blank the news after I heard about that terrible earthquake.
A.explain: Simple past is watched. Watch is present. Watching is continuous. Watches is third-person present.

A.q: When the teacher blank to class, all the students stopped talking.
A.explain: Simple past in time clause is came. Come is present. Comes is third person. Coming is continuous.

A.q: The fans blank angry when their favorite star canceled the concert.
A.explain: Simple past is got. Get is present. Gets is third person. Getting is continuous.

A.q: We blank when a dog suddenly ran in front of us.
A.explain: Simple past is screamed. Scream is present. Screaming is continuous. Screams is third person.

A.q: I blank on the project for hours before I got a message that it was canceled.
A.explain: Simple past is worked. Work is present. Working is continuous. Works is third person.

A.q: The mother blank lunch before her kids came back from school.
A.explain: Simple past is cooked. Cook is present. Cooking is continuous. Cooks is third person.

A.q: When the police blank the thief, he confessed to all his crimes.
A.explain: Simple past is arrested. Arrest is present. Arresting is continuous. Arrests is third person.

A.q: Correct: When you start working as a nurse?
options: When did you start working as a nurse?
When you start working as a nurse often?
When did you started working as a nurse daily?
When you started working as a nurse regularly?
A.explain: Questions need Did + base verb. Missing Did, Did + started, and no auxiliary are wrong.

A.q: Correct: Did you visited your grandmother in the hospital last weekend?
options: Did you visit your grandmother in the hospital?
Did you visited your grandmother in the hospital often?
Did you visit your grandmother in the hospital daily?
You visited your grandmother in the hospital regularly?
A.explain: Did + base verb is correct. Did + visited is double past. Other forms miss the structure.

A.q: Correct: The doctor check my blood pressure yesterday.
options: The doctor checked my blood pressure yesterday
The doctor check my blood pressure yesterday often
The doctor checks my blood pressure yesterday daily
The doctor checking my blood pressure yesterday regularly
A.explain: Simple past is checked. Check is present. Checks is third-person present. Checking is continuous.

A.q: Correct: Last week the nurse take care of ten patients in one day.
options: Last week the nurse took care of ten patients
Last week the nurse take care of ten patients often
Last week the nurse takes care of ten patients daily
Last week the nurse taking care of ten patients regularly
A.explain: Simple past is took. Take is present. Takes is third person. Taking is continuous.

A.q: Correct: The hospital open a new emergency room last year.
options: The hospital opened a new emergency room last year
The hospital open a new emergency room last year often
The hospital opens a new emergency room last year daily
The hospital opening a new emergency room last year regularly
A.explain: Simple past is opened. Open is present. Opens is third person. Opening is continuous.

A.q: Correct: We don't needed an appointment for the flu vaccine last winter.
options: We didn't need an appointment for the flu vaccine
We don't needed an appointment for the flu vaccine often
We didn't needed an appointment for the flu vaccine daily
We don't need an appointment for the flu vaccine regularly
A.explain: Negative past is didn't need. Don't needed, didn't needed, and don't need (present) are wrong for past.

A.q: Correct: The patient didn't went to the pharmacy after the appointment.
options: The patient didn't go to the pharmacy
The patient didn't went to the pharmacy often
The patient don't go to the pharmacy daily
The patient wasn't go to the pharmacy regularly
A.explain: Didn't + base verb is correct. Didn't went is double past. Don't go is present. Wasn't go is incorrect.

A.q: Correct: We wasn't ready when the ambulance arrived.
options: We weren't ready when the ambulance arrived
We wasn't ready when the ambulance arrived often
We aren't ready when the ambulance arrived daily
We didn't ready when the ambulance arrived regularly
A.explain: Plural needs weren't. Wasn't is singular. Aren't is present. Didn't ready is incorrect.

A.q: Which time-clause pair is both in simple past?
options: Kate broke her leg when she fell down
Kate break her leg when she fell down often
Kate broke her leg when she fall down daily
Kate breaking her leg when she fell down regularly
A.explain: Both verbs need simple past: broke and fell. Break, fall, and breaking are wrong forms.

A.q: Which practice item is correct for plural past?
options: My brothers and I were in Dubai in 2000
My brothers and I was in Dubai in 2000 often
My brothers and I there were in Dubai in 2000 daily
My brothers and I there was in Dubai in 2000 regularly
A.explain: Plural subject needs were. Was is singular. There were and there was are existential forms.

A.q: Which time-clause verb is simple past after before?
options: The mother cooked lunch before her kids came
The mother cook lunch before her kids came often
The mother cooked lunch before her kids come daily
The mother cooking lunch before her kids came regularly
A.explain: Both verbs need simple past: cooked and came. Cook, come, and cooking are wrong forms.

A.q: Which question form avoids double past?
options: Did you visit your grandmother last weekend?
Did you visited your grandmother last weekend often?
Did you visit your grandmother last weekend daily?
You visited your grandmother last weekend regularly?
A.explain: Did + base verb is correct. Did + visited is double past. Other forms miss the auxiliary.

A.q: Which negative past avoids double marking?
options: The patient didn't go to the pharmacy
The patient didn't went to the pharmacy often
The patient don't go to the pharmacy daily
The patient wasn't go to the pharmacy regularly
A.explain: Didn't + base verb is correct. Didn't went is double past. Don't go is present. Wasn't go is incorrect.

A.q: Which plural form is correct with past be?
options: We weren't ready when the ambulance arrived
We wasn't ready when the ambulance arrived often
We aren't ready when the ambulance arrived daily
We didn't ready when the ambulance arrived regularly
A.explain: Plural needs weren't. Wasn't is singular. Aren't is present. Didn't ready is incorrect.

A.q: Which simple-past form fits the time clause when?
options: We screamed when a dog suddenly ran in front of us
We scream when a dog suddenly ran in front of us often
We screaming when a dog suddenly ran in front of us daily
We screams when a dog suddenly ran in front of us regularly
A.explain: Simple past is screamed. Scream is present. Screaming is continuous. Screams is third person.

A.q: Which error item needs the past of open?
options: The hospital opened a new emergency room last year
The hospital open a new emergency room last year often
The hospital opens a new emergency room last year daily
The hospital opening a new emergency room last year regularly
A.explain: Simple past is opened. Open is present. Opens is third person. Opening is continuous.

A.q: Which time-clause verb after after is simple past?
options: I watched the news after I heard about the earthquake
I watch the news after I heard about the earthquake often
I watching the news after I heard about the earthquake daily
I watches the news after I heard about the earthquake regularly
A.explain: Simple past is watched. Watch is present. Watching is continuous. Watches is third person.

A.q: Which error needs the past of take?
options: Last week the nurse took care of ten patients
Last week the nurse take care of ten patients often
Last week the nurse takes care of ten patients daily
Last week the nurse taking care of ten patients regularly
A.explain: Simple past is took. Take is present. Takes is third person. Taking is continuous.

A.q: Yesterday, ___ a huge accident on the highway.
A.explain: The subject is singular: a huge accident. The correct past form is there was.

A.q: ___ many students in the class?
A.explain: The question form is Were there + plural noun. Students is plural, so the correct question is Were there many students in the class?

A.q: Were there many students in the class? Yes, ___.
A.explain: The short answer repeats the structure: Yes, there were. There was is singular, and they were does not match the there construction.

A.q: My friends ___ at my house last weekend.
A.explain: Friends is plural and the time is last weekend, so the correct past form is were all.

A.q: I ___ dinner yesterday.
A.explain: Past simple negative uses didn't + base verb. The correct form is didn't have.

A.q: What ___ you ___ yesterday?
A.explain: Past simple Wh-questions use: Wh-word + did + subject + base verb. The correct form is What did you have yesterday?

A.q: Which question matches: My friends were at the party yesterday.
A.explain: Friends is plural, so the past be verb is were. The correct question is Where were your friends yesterday?

A.q: I waited for you ___ the shop closed, so I went home.
A.explain: Until shows that the waiting continued up to the moment the shop closed. The correct sentence is I waited for you until the shop closed.

A.q: When I ___ a bad grade in the exam, I decided to study harder.
A.explain: The sentence is past simple, so the correct form is got. Get is present, getting is continuous, and was get is incorrect.

A.q: In 1928, Alexander Fleming ___ penicillin.
A.explain: This is a single completed past event, so simple past is correct: discovered. Used to is for repeated past habits or states, not one-time events.
